enforcement_points.component: Broker request stage, before routing to the resource layer: verifies the agent's own broker credential, resolves the grant named by the request's task reference, reads the grant's session live, returns the session principal with the agent's workload; no live session is a native denial; a grant for another agent is denied

Enrollment registry lookup by the realm, the agent's broker workload, and the agent ID that the presentation names, independent of the SAML sign-in; a workload with more than one enrollment in force is a configuration error
Broker mapping stage, mapping revision pact-saml-1, baseline HTTP mapping

Live read of the SP session record for the approved paths /attributes/environment/principal_id and /attributes/environment/idp_realm; a directory adapter for membership facts when a contract requires them
Installed checks native-delegation-v1 and execution-identity-v1, with the mandatory protocol checks
The SP's existing access policy for the requested records, invoked with the session principal and never the broker's identity
Broker outcome writer, after execution; each authorization and execution report references an immutable native record of the actual executor identity

bypass_paths.path: Grant creation and management routes of the portal, reached with an agent credential and no user session
bypass_paths.evidence: These routes accept only a live SPSession as authentication and reject an agent credential (SB-8); planned case SAML-10, no fixture file yet

bypass_paths.path: Broker routes and methods outside the two protected routes, including every operation with side effects, reached with a valid agent credential, an enrolled agent and a live grant
bypass_paths.evidence: The broker's agent-facing route table serves only the two protected routes (SB-20); planned case SAML-11, no fixture file yet

bypass_paths.path: The same portal resources reached directly by the user's own browser session, with no agent involved
bypass_paths.evidence: Native user access under native authorization, not an agent request path; excluded in unsupported_forms (the user's own access)

bypass_paths.path: An agent using a copy of the user's session credential or of a SAML assertion against portal routes
bypass_paths.evidence: SB-3 forbids the SP to hand either to the agent but a user-side copy cannot be controlled; excluded in unsupported_forms (assertion and session credential export)

bypass_paths.path: SAML sign-in (assertion consumer) and single logout endpoints of the SP
bypass_paths.evidence: Assertion validation stays in the SP's SAML implementation (SB-1); what the adapter does with the resulting sessions is covered by the cases SAML-01, SAML-02, SAML-04 and SAML-05

bypass_paths.path: Native administrative paths that create, change or revoke enrollments, grants or sessions
bypass_paths.evidence: Governed by the environment's own administrative controls, not an agent request path

unsupported_forms: Universal unattended SAML agent login: a request with no live SPSession has no principal (case SAML-09); the Enhanced Client or Proxy profile and any other SAML profile or binding used by an agent as a SAML party are not claimed

Delegation supplied by SAML itself: the only delegation read is the TaskGrant created by an authenticated portal action; no delegation, proxying or act-as meaning is read from any SAML message or extension

Assertion export to the agent, export of the SP session credential to the agent, and the user's own direct access: the SP hands the agent neither, and a copy a user makes or the user's own access is outside the claim

IdP-initiated agent sessions: an unsolicited Response can at most establish the user's SP session, never a grant or an agent task, because a grant exists only through a portal action in a live session

Agents that share one broker credential: each agent has its own broker credential, the default of identity-mapping section 5, and a workload with more than one enrollment in force is a configuration error
Operations with side effects, and every route other than the two in protected_routes: transactions, budgets and idempotency need C15, which is not used, and a route not listed is not claimed

Membership, role and account-state facts taken from the assertion, the SPSession or authn_instant: such facts come only from a directory adapter with its own observation time, and no directory adapter profile has landed
A requirement on how recently the user authenticated: authn_instant is not a freshness time and no baseline check consumes it
An SP that has no task broker: there is no TaskGrant and no authenticated portal action to create one
The final semantics of authority_ref: they wait for the delegation binding model

freshness.source: Enrollment registry (agent and key binding status)

live_check.endpoint_class: local lookup of the SP's session record, on the authoritative copy

residual_limits: Post-read: data already returned to the agent is not recalled by a later logout, expiry or grant revocation, and an executed operation is not undone by revoking its receipt; no egress, output or data-use control is claimed and a required runtime fact is attested-only; disclosed here with no bound

Revocation propagation, SP session: a logout, a termination by the SP and expiry are seen at the next read of the session record and every grant of that session is then unusable; zero within the SP's consistency domain

Revocation propagation, identity provider: a session that ends at the identity provider reaches this profile only as a logout request at the SP or as a new authentication by the user, otherwise the SP session continues until its own end, and the logout protocol is a SHOULD for the session authority with a PartialLogout status for unreachable participants (SAML Core section 3.7.3.2); bounded by the session expires_at and the grant expires_at, and not otherwise

Revocation propagation, grants and enrollment: a revoked grant, or a binding revoked or marked compromised, prevents later admissions in the gateway's consistency domain; the binding is read for each evaluation; zero within each store's own consistency

In-flight operations: a read that has begun when the session ends is not cancelled by this profile; session and grant are read immediately before execution starts and after that the broker's native cancellation semantics apply, which the broker documents

Name reuse: the SAML texts read do not say whether an identity provider may issue a persistent NameID value again to another subject after deleting one, so a reused value could map to an existing principal; disclosed here and open

Forged portal action: a browser can be induced to make the portal action that creates a grant without the user's intent; the SP applies its own request-forgery defences, which this profile does not specify; disclosed here with no bound
Re-stamp detection on session claims: the two session claims carry no SourceRef, so the monotonic guard does not compare them and the integration rests on the gateway's own clock; disclosed here
